modules.title: Welcome & The Wheel of Life
modules.description: Understand the full picture of your life before we dive into finances. The Wheel of Life helps you identify where you are now and where you want to go.

lessons.title: Welcome to the Course
lessons.description: An overview of what you'll learn and how to get the most out of this program.
lessons.notes:
Welcome! In this course you will:

- Discover the Wheel of Life framework and how finances fit into every area
- Build a clear picture of your current financial health
- Create a personalized financial plan aligned with your life goals
- Develop habits that sustain long-term financial wellbeing

Before we dive into numbers and strategies, we start with the big picture: your whole life.

lessons.title: What Is the Wheel of Life?
lessons.description: Explore the eight areas of life and score where you are today.
lessons.notes:
The Wheel of Life is a powerful self-assessment tool that looks at eight key life areas:

1. **Career & Work** – Are you fulfilled and growing professionally?
2. **Money & Finances** – Do you feel secure and in control of your finances?
3. **Health & Fitness** – Are you caring for your physical and mental wellbeing?
4. **Family & Friends** – How strong and nourishing are your relationships?
5. **Romance & Partnership** – Is your intimate relationship thriving?
6. **Personal Growth** – Are you learning, evolving, and becoming your best self?
7. **Fun & Recreation** – Do you have joy, hobbies, and rest in your life?
8. **Physical Environment** – Does your home and workspace support your goals?

Rate each area from 1–10 and draw your wheel. The areas that are low often have a direct connection to your financial patterns.

questions.question: How many areas does the Wheel of Life assess?
questions.explanation: The Wheel of Life has 8 areas: Career, Money, Health, Family, Romance, Personal Growth, Fun, and Physical Environment.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of completing a Wheel of Life assessment?
options: To get a visual snapshot of life balance and identify low-scoring areas
questions.explanation: The Wheel of Life gives you a visual snapshot of how balanced your life feels across key areas, helping you identify where to focus your energy.

lessons.title: How Money Affects Every Spoke of the Wheel
lessons.description: Understand the deep connection between financial health and all eight life areas.
lessons.notes:
Money is not isolated — it touches every area of your Wheel of Life:

- **Career:** Your income, benefits, and career choices are directly tied to financial decisions.
- **Health:** Financial stress is one of the leading causes of poor health outcomes.
- **Family:** Financial disagreements are a top cause of relationship strain.
- **Personal Growth:** Learning costs money; financial freedom creates time to grow.
- **Fun:** Experiences and hobbies require discretionary income.
- **Environment:** Your home, neighbourhood, and workspace reflect and affect your finances.

This is why we start with the whole wheel — not just the money spoke.

questions.question: Financial stress is primarily linked to which life area of the Wheel?
options: Multiple areas including Health, Family, and Career
questions.explanation: Financial stress affects many areas simultaneously — it impacts health, strains relationships, limits career options, and reduces quality of life across the board.

modules.title: Financial Foundations
modules.description: Establish the core financial knowledge you need: income, expenses, assets, liabilities, and your net worth.

lessons.title: Your Financial Snapshot: Net Worth
lessons.description: Learn to calculate your net worth — the starting point of every financial plan.
lessons.notes:
**Net Worth = Assets − Liabilities**

**Assets** (what you own):
- Cash and bank accounts
- Investments (shares, super, managed funds)
- Property
- Vehicles and other valuables

**Liabilities** (what you owe):
- Mortgage
- Car loans
- Credit card balances
- Personal loans
- HECS/student debt

Your net worth is not a judgement — it is a starting point. Many people begin with a negative net worth and build significant wealth over time.

questions.question: If your assets total $350,000 and your liabilities total $180,000, what is your net worth?
questions.explanation: $350,000 − $180,000 = $170,000. Net worth is always assets minus liabilities.

lessons.title: Understanding Income & Cash Flow
lessons.description: Map your income streams and understand the difference between cash flow and wealth.
lessons.notes:
**Types of Income:**

- **Active Income:** Wages, salary, freelance fees — requires your time
- **Passive Income:** Rent, dividends, royalties — earns while you sleep
- **Portfolio Income:** Capital gains from selling investments

**Cash Flow = Money In − Money Out**

Positive cash flow means you have money left over each period. This surplus is what you use to build wealth.

Key principle: **It is not how much you earn, it is how much you keep and grow.**

questions.question: Which type of income earns money without requiring your active time?
questions.explanation: Passive income (rent, dividends, royalties) generates money without requiring your direct time and effort.

modules.title: Budgeting & Spending Plans
modules.description: Create a spending plan that funds your whole Wheel of Life — not just bills.

lessons.title: The 50/30/20 Rule
lessons.description: A simple framework for allocating your after-tax income.
lessons.notes:
The 50/30/20 rule divides your after-tax income into three buckets:

- **50% Needs** – Housing, utilities, groceries, transport, insurance
- **30% Wants** – Dining out, entertainment, hobbies, subscriptions
- **20% Savings & Debt Repayment** – Emergency fund, investments, extra loan payments

This is a starting framework. Your actual percentages will depend on your income, location, and Wheel of Life priorities.

questions.question: In the 50/30/20 rule, what percentage is allocated to savings and debt repayment?
questions.explanation: The 20% bucket covers savings, investments, and extra debt repayments — the wealth-building portion of your budget.

modules.title: Goal Setting & Financial Planning
modules.description: Use your Wheel of Life scores to set meaningful financial goals and build a roadmap.

lessons.title: Connecting Your Wheel Scores to Financial Goals
lessons.description: Turn your Wheel of Life assessment into specific, funded goals.
lessons.notes:
Each low-scoring area of your Wheel of Life likely has a financial component:

- **Health score 4/10?** → Budget for gym membership, better nutrition, or health appointments
- **Fun score 3/10?** → Allocate discretionary spending for experiences and hobbies
- **Career score 5/10?** → Invest in professional development or education
- **Environment score 4/10?** → Plan for home improvements or relocation savings

**SMART Financial Goals:**
- **Specific:** Save $10,000 emergency fund
- **Measurable:** $833/month for 12 months
- **Achievable:** Fits within your cash flow
- **Relevant:** Aligned with your Wheel of Life priorities
- **Time-bound:** Completed by [date]

questions.question: What does the 'M' in SMART goals stand for?
questions.explanation: Measurable means your goal has a specific number or milestone so you can track progress.
